issues.jp_before: お客様[きゃくさま]のお名前[なまえ]は、何[なん]と{おっしゃいます|kg-son-special}か。
issues.problem: English 'How do you say your name, sir? (What is your name?)' was a literal, unnatural rendering of the set phrase.
issues.action: English changed to 'May I ask your name, sir?'.

issues.jp_before: どうぞ、温[あたた]かいうちに{召[め]し上[あ]がってください|kg-son-special}。
issues.problem: お召し上がりください is an equally natural answer with the same meaning but was not listed.
issues.action: Added お召[め]し上[あ]がりください as an alternative.

issues.jp_before: こちらの資料[しりょう]を{ご覧[らん]になってください|kg-son-special}。
issues.problem: ご覧ください is the more common equivalent and was not listed.
issues.action: Added ご覧[らん]ください as an alternative.

issues.jp_before: 部長[ぶちょう]は昔[むかし]、どんなお仕事[しごと]を{なさっていました|kg-son-special}か。
issues.problem: English 'What kind of work did you do in the past, sir? (to the manager)' forced a direct-address reading with a parenthetical note; the Japanese is a plain third-person question.
issues.action: English changed to 'What kind of work did the manager do in the past?'.

issues.jp_before: 社長[しゃちょう]は、どうして急[きゅう]に出張[しゅっちょう]を{なさる|kg-son-special}ことにしたのですか。
issues.problem: The honorific なさる followed by a plain ことにした for the same respected subject is inconsistent keigo that a teacher would not model.
issues.action: Changed to …ことになったのですか, with the English 'Why is the president suddenly going on a business trip?'.

issues.jp_before: 先生[せんせい]、もし…{ご存[ぞん]じなら|kg-son-special}… (was: 先生[せんせい]が{ご存[ぞん]じなら|kg-son-special}、教[おし]えてもらえませんか。)
issues.problem: もらえませんか is too casual for a request to a professor, and the English 'could you ask them to tell us?' was a forced reading.
issues.action: Rewrote it as 先生[せんせい]、もし{ご存[ぞん]じなら}、教[おし]えていただけませんか。 with the English 'Professor, if you know, could you please tell me?'.

issues.jp_before: 先生[せんせい]は、あの方[かた]を{ご存[ぞん]じですか|kg-son-special}。
issues.problem: Near-duplicate of 先生は、この店をご存じですか (same frame), and the ご存じ items were already almost all questions.
issues.action: Replaced it with a statement: 社長[しゃちょう]は、私[わたし]の父[ちち]のことをよく{ご存[ぞん]じです}。 / 'The president knows my father well.', distractors 存じております / 存じ上げております / 存じ上げます.
